retraction.retracted_claim: u11-data.js - sourceClass + settlement fields on every attempt and meter; R().human/deText keep UI copy clean
retraction.why_the_claim_was_false: Both misattributed and mischaracterized. R.human and R.deText are not in u11-data.js - `grep -n deText u11-data.js` returns no hits. They live in _shared/usage-data.js:921 and :927 and are reached through u11-widgets.js:24 `function R() { return window.USrender; }`. And R.human is `String(s).replace(/_/g, ' ')` - a render-time underscore-to-space substitution on the raw token, not normalization. This file's sibling concedes the point: event-schema-delta.json purpose_taxonomy.rendering says 'No renderer label map exists; purposes render via R().human()', which is why renaming the purpose taxonomy required zero renderer edits.
retraction.consequence: Because R.human strips underscores at render time, the harness's 'underscores === 0' assertion in all 40 matrix cases cannot detect raw enum leakage into user-visible copy - a de-underscored raw token passes that check.

source_citation_policy: Source citations into u11-prism.html, u11-data.js, u11-widgets.js, u11-rundetail.js and u11-context.js name a symbol, identifier or exact string rather than a line number. Those five files were under concurrent edit on 2026-08-18 - u11-data.js moved twice while this repair was being written - so a line number here would be wrong by the time it was read. Line numbers are retained only for files that are stable in this pass: everything under Plans/ and under _shared/. Text preserved inside a `retraction` or `retracted_claim` object is left exactly as it was written, line numbers included, because its purpose is to record what a document said on a past date.
